architecture_principles: a discovered material regularity is only usable inside the chemistry family in which it was measured
a scientific applicability boundary is executable code, not prompt advice
the language model may criticize the rule and may not override it
value of information is computed by a deterministic tool over the admissible set only
held-out result data are structurally removed before any payload is assembled
every gate decision carries a machine-readable reason and is serialized with the run

arm_difference_declaration.forbidden_confound: Hiding applicability information from V5_NO_GATE while showing it to V5_FULL is prohibited by protocol v1.1.
held_identical: model endpoint and stage model assignment
evidence access profile and filtered evidence state
raw assess_shared_shape_applicability outputs for every candidate
the full inadmissible-card list and its machine-readable reasons
VOI implementation, weights and tie epsilon
arm_difference_declaration.information_parity_evidence: build_pre_enforcement_payload() takes no arm argument, and its SHA-256 is written into every run as pre_enforcement_payload_sha256. The two arms must report the same hash.
arm_difference_declaration.only_intended_difference: whether the identical chemistry-domain applicability audit is enforced as hard experiment-card admissibility before VOI and at freeze
arm_difference_declaration.payload_consequence: Both arms receive the same audit, the same per-candidate applicability outputs and the same inadmissible-card list. V5_NO_GATE marks the audit advisory and keeps every card selectable; V5_FULL marks it binding and removes the inadmissible cards from the ranked set.

candidate_space.rationale: V5 reuses the byte-identical V3/V4 lattice so that the measured change is the chemistry-domain constraint, not the search space.

architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> mandatory chemistry-audited local science tool -> deterministic chemistry-domain applicability audit (identical and model-visible in both arms) -> enforcement (V5_FULL only) -> VOI over the selectable set -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze

rules: M-HOLD-120 is admissible: it measures thermal-hold drift directly and does not use the shared thermal-response shape.
M-REPEAT is admissible: it measures realization/state spread directly.
M-SWEEP is admissible: it is the direct verification measurement for a chemistry-shifted candidate.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use equal to allowed_with_state_anchor, or when configs/verified_shape_transfer.json records a completed direct sweep for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification. This is deterministic inadmissibility, not a VOI penalty and not prompt advice.

architecture.claim_boundary: V5.0.0 selects an experiment from pre-result evidence under an outcome-blind runtime with a deterministic chemistry-domain admissibility constraint. A V5 result is evidence about executable scientific constraints on measurement choice. It is not a wet-lab result and does not claim that the historical decision used this ranking.
architecture.manuscript_boundary: V5 run results must not be written into manuscript/MAIN_TEXT_V5.md or manuscript/SUPPLEMENTARY_INFORMATION_V5.md until the run series is audited and explicitly frozen by the author.
architecture.name: PUR_NEW_CHEMISTRY_GATED_EXPERIMENT_SELECTION_AGENT_V5
non_goals: adding a language model to compute value of information or admissibility
adding Agent roles beyond planner, tools, proposer, skeptic, robustness adjudicator, judge and freeze
re-running, rewriting or reinterpreting the frozen V4 series

primary_arms.role: advice-only control isolating the incremental effect of turning identical scientific applicability information into an executable hard constraint
prospective chemistry-aware Agent V5 with executable scientific constraints

architecture.purpose: Test whether an experimentally discovered material regularity and its chemistry-domain boundary can be executed as a hard scientific constraint on which measurement an outcome-blind Agent is allowed to select.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode and the scientific question the next experiment must answer, and request the evidence needed to judge experiments rather than formulations
execute read-only scientific tools. The chemistry-audited local rheology summary is mandatory and is forced into the trace whether or not the planner requested it.

deterministic, non-LLM measurement-applicability audit. Computed once per run without reference to the arm, fully visible to the model in both arms, serialized in full, and never produced by a model stage.
V5_FULL only. Converts the identical audit into hard admissibility before VOI ranking and again at freeze. It cannot be overridden by any model stage.
propose the experiment with the highest scientific information value from the cards present in the payload
attack the proposed experiment on hypothesis coverage, confounding, interpretability and whether its falsification criterion can actually be met
adjudicate whether the proposed experiment survives the reported weight sensitivity and the strongest objection
commit to one experiment card present in the payload, or abstain, and state its acceptance and falsification criteria
programmatically validate and freeze the experiment card. A selection outside the admissible set is rejected at freeze rather than repaired.

architecture.supersedes_nothing: V5 is a new prospective runtime. configs/agent_v4.json, scripts/run_agent_v4.py, prompts/agent_v4_*.txt, src/pur_new/voi.py and every frozen V3/V4 run record remain unchanged and are not reinterpreted by V5.

voi_tool.explicitly_not: distance to any held-out formulation. No target coordinate enters any component, weight or tie-break.
voi_tool.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk
voi_tool.name: score_experiment_cards

decision_stability_sent_to_model.evaluated_over: the selectable experiment cards of this arm
decision_stability_sent_to_model.metric_is_not: model confidence; posterior probability; calibrated expected information
decision_stability_sent_to_model.voi_formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.

evidence_policy.description: For prospective/blind Agent evaluation. The Agent may see original-system measurements and external analogue evidence, but not the target validation formulation identity, its wet-lab outcome, or any outcome-derived labels.

judge_normalized.acceptance_criterion: Accept the transferred H-CORE baseline for subsequent modifier comparisons if the arithmetic mean SI_15_60 across at least two independent preparations is from 7.51% through 11.51%, inclusive, corresponding to the E1-based 9.51% prediction within the declared 2.00-percentage-point resolution.
judge_normalized.chemistry_support_statement: S1C09 remains inside the measured unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI chemistry family. The primary observable does not depend on any transferred rheological regularity, shared thermal-response shape, regression, or M-ANCHOR reconstruction; it is measured directly in the selected candidate. The E1 comparator is from the same broad chemistry family, but transfer from the E1 NCO:OH 1.7 core to the E2-derived NCO:OH 1.8 core is precisely the formulation-level assumption being tested. Therefore the result can establish an E2-core rheological drift baseline, not a molecular mechanism.
judge_normalized.falsification_criterion: If the arithmetic mean SI_15_60 is below 7.51%, falsify H-CORE's registered 9.51% quantitative prediction for the undiluted E2-derived core in the specified low-drift direction. If the mean is above 11.51%, reject the same H-CORE quantitative prediction in the high-drift direction. Neither outcome by itself falsifies H-RESIN or H-DUAL because S1C09 contains no modifier axis.
judge_normalized.next_experiment_if_falsified: Run S1C41::M-HOLD-120 under preparation, dehydration, storage, and prior melt-residence histories matched to S1C09, and define its linear-dilution comparator from the measured S1C09 mean rather than from E1. If the S1C09 repeats are discordant at a scale exceeding 2.00 percentage points, first repeat S1C09::M-HOLD-120 with at least three controlled independent preparations.
judge_normalized.primary_observable: The preregistered arithmetic mean of repeat-level SI_15_60 = 100 × (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, measured directly during a 120 C hold using at least two independent preparations; viscosity is recorded at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min.
judge_normalized.rationale: S1C09::M-HOLD-120 is the defensible first experiment because it directly establishes the previously unmeasured E2-core drift coefficient and prevents an E1-to-E2 baseline difference from being misassigned to resin suppression. It is a state-control experiment rather than a mitigation test: S1C41 remains the appropriate subsequent dual-axis hold, followed by acrylic-only S1C39 if separation of H-RESIN from H-DUAL is required.
judge_normalized.stage_disagreements_resolved: I follow the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator rather than the Proposer on experiment ordering. The Proposer's S1C41::M-HOLD-120 is the stable deterministic top-ranked mitigation card, and the weight sweep never displaced it, but its 7.61% comparator assumes that E1's single NCO:OH 1.7 hold coefficient transfers to an unmeasured E2-derived NCO:OH 1.8 core. That prerequisite is absent from the VOI score. Measuring S1C09 first removes the baseline ambiguity before attributing any modified-formulation result to superlinear suppression. The advisory chemistry audit raises no objection to S1C09::M-HOLD-120.

uncertainty_decomposition.evidence_coverage_uncertainty: The E2-derived reactive core has no prior thermal-hold trajectory, while E1 and E5 each have only one original hold run. This experiment directly fills the missing E2-core baseline but provides no evidence about either resin axis.
uncertainty_decomposition.extrapolation_uncertainty: Chemistry-domain extrapolation is low because S1C09 is in the unmodified measured family and the observable is direct. The important remaining extrapolation is the E1-to-E2 stoichiometric and core-composition transfer embodied in the 9.51% comparator; this experiment tests rather than assumes that transfer.
uncertainty_decomposition.measurement_uncertainty: M-HOLD-120 directly measures SI_15_60; the declared discrimination resolution is 2.00 percentage points. At least two independent preparations are required, and the arithmetic mean is frozen as the threshold statistic while repeat-level values and spread must also be reported.
uncertainty_decomposition.realization_state_uncertainty: Substantial: prior E2 preparations showed viscosity-level CVs of approximately 46-58% and a 3.57-fold max/min ratio at 120 C. Preparation, dehydration, storage, and prior melt-residence histories must therefore be frozen and recorded, although M-HOLD-120 does not itself control those variables.

planner.chemistry_support_statement: The reported local thermal-response regularity was measured in the original reactive PUR formulation family represented by E1, E2, and E3, with a separate E1 +P chemical-perturbation check; E2 is the registered reactive-core anchor. An experiment introducing acrylic-like and/or minor tackifier-like modifiers would retain the E2 core but would not remain strictly inside the directly measured composition family. The shared thermal-response shape must therefore be audited for the concrete candidate, and a direct 80–130 °C sweep is required if applicability is not established.
planner.failure_mode: Excessive viscosity growth during prolonged isothermal melt residence at 120 °C, with the mechanism of drift suppression versus acceleration unresolved.
planner.failure_mode_evidence: The original E5 thermal-hold run increased by 51.54% from 15 to 60 min at 120 °C, compared with 9.51% for the least-drifting original reference E1 over the same measured window.
planner.least_resolved_justification: The local temperature coordinate is covered by multiple six-point 80–130 °C sweeps, whereas the isothermal coordinate has only one four-point 120 °C trajectory for E1 and one for E5, with no repeat hold runs and no measured trajectory for E2 or for either registered modifier axis. The large E1/E5 contrast therefore establishes the failure mode but does not resolve its formulation dependence.
measurement_requirements: Measure the primary mechanistic observable directly with M-HOLD-120: viscosity at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min during a 120 °C hold, using at least two independent preparations.
Report SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15 as a percentage for each repeat and its repeat-level spread; do not extrapolate beyond the measured 15–60 min decision window.

For every tested composition, calculate the frozen H-CORE comparator E1_drift × phi_r from the independently determined reactive mass fraction, then compare the measured drift with both the linear-dilution prediction and the H-RESIN threshold of less than half that prediction, subject to the declared 2 percentage-point discrimination resolution.

To adjudicate H-DUAL rather than only H-CORE versus H-RESIN, include matched acrylic-only and acrylic-plus-minor-tackifier experiments with the same reactive core and otherwise controlled preparation and hold history.

Record and control preparation, dehydration, storage, and melt-residence history because E2 nominal repeats show viscosity-level CVs of approximately 46–58% and max/min ratios of 2.80–3.57 across 80–130 °C.

Do not infer candidate viscosity level or temperature response from the local shared shape until chemistry applicability has been established. If it is not established, run a fresh 80–130 °C sweep in 10 °C increments; otherwise use a 110 °C anchor with direct verification at 120 and 130 °C.
Preserve the source viscosity unit as unknown unless source-level evidence supplies it; comparisons may use matched-window relative changes without inventing a unit.
planner.scientific_question: For an E2-core resin-modified formulation, is the 15–60 min viscosity drift at 120 °C consistent with simple reactive-mass dilution, or is it suppressed substantially below the H-CORE prediction; and, when acrylic-only and dual-axis formulations are compared, is a nonzero minor tackifier required to reach the low-drift regime? This separates H-CORE from H-RESIN and can also distinguish H-DUAL from a general resin-suppression mechanism.

proposer.chemistry_support_assessment: S1C41 is outside the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI family in which the shared thermal-response shape was measured. However, M-HOLD-120 directly observes matched-window drift and does not reconstruct it from that shared shape, so the unverified shape transfer does not compromise the primary observable. No M-ANCHOR-based inference of viscosity level or temperature response should be made for this chemistry before a direct sweep verifies transferability.
hypotheses_not_separated: H-RESIN vs H-DUAL; both predict approximately 3.80% drift for this dual-axis composition, so an acrylic-only hold would be required to test whether the minor tackifier is specifically necessary

outcome_interpretation.if_acceptance_criterion_met: Drift below 3.80% across at least two repeats is less than half the 7.61% linear-dilution prediction. It falsifies H-CORE at this composition and supports superlinear resin suppression. It is also consistent with H-DUAL, but cannot distinguish H-DUAL from H-RESIN because both predict the same low-drift outcome here.
outcome_interpretation.if_falsification_criterion_met: Drift at or above 7.61% falsifies H-RESIN's superlinear-suppression prediction and is inconsistent with the low-drift prediction assigned to H-DUAL for an active minor-tackifier axis. Agreement near 7.61% supports H-CORE's linear-dilution rule; a result substantially above 7.61% would instead indicate that neither simple dilution nor the registered suppression rules adequately describe the formulation.
outcome_interpretation.if_intermediate: A result from 3.80% to below 7.61% indicates partial suppression but meets neither preregistered decision threshold. It would not decisively select H-CORE or H-RESIN and would still leave H-RESIN versus H-DUAL unresolved; repeat-level spread and controlled process history would be essential for interpretation.

proposer.primary_observable: SI_15_60 = (eta_60 - eta_15) / eta_15, percent, measured directly during a 120 C hold at 15, 30, 45, and 60 min across at least two independent preparations

ranked_alternatives.why_lower_value: Deterministically tied, but uses 17.5% acrylic rather than the smaller sufficient 15% intervention and has a slightly narrower H-CORE versus suppression prediction gap.
Deterministically tied and located at a directly commensurate 20% acrylic evidence anchor, but imposes greater modifier burden without improving hypothesis-pair coverage or measurement directness.
Deterministically tied, but the 22.5% acrylic loading is a larger departure from the characterized core and further narrows the prediction gap without adding discrimination.
Deterministically tied and externally supported at 25% acrylic, but has the largest modifier burden and the smallest H-CORE versus suppression prediction gap among the tied cards.
Measures the same direct drift observable, but its 7.5% tackifier level lies above the repeated 4.8-6.4% support cluster, creating extrapolation risk and a lower VOI score.

Would directly verify temperature-response shape in the modified chemistry, but its fitted slope does not discriminate any registered drift-mechanism pair and is less relevant to the declared thermal-hold failure mode.

proposer.reasoning: The selected card directly measures the least-resolved and decision-critical isothermal drift coordinate, separates two of the three registered hypothesis pairs, stays within both supported modifier regions, and avoids reliance on an unverified thermal-shape model. Its main limitation is moderate process-state risk and inability to separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL, so preparation, dehydration, storage, and prior melt-residence history must be controlled and recorded for both repeats.
proposer.tie_break_justification: All five cards have identical VOI components and keep both modifier axes within the supported regions. S1C41 is selected because it uses the smallest total modifier burden in the tied set—15% acrylic-like modifier plus the directly supported 5% minor-tackifier level—while retaining a 3.80 percentage-point separation between the H-CORE and low-drift predictions, larger than the declared 2.00-point measurement resolution. This follows the minimum-sufficient-intervention policy without treating proximity to an external analogue as an outcome predictor.

robustness_adjudication.change_from_proposal: Changed from S1C41::M-HOLD-120 to the reactive-core-only S1C09::M-HOLD-120 to measure the previously unobserved E2-core drift coefficient before interpreting resin-modified drift against a linear-dilution comparator. The chemistry audit does not invalidate direct M-HOLD-120 measurements; it only prohibits unsupported shared-shape reconstruction for modified chemistry. The switch is therefore driven by baseline validity, not weight sensitivity or chemistry-domain admissibility.
residual_decision_risk: A single reactive-core-only hold does not measure the resin-modified response; matched S1C41 testing remains necessary afterward.
H-RESIN versus H-DUAL remains unresolved without the matched acrylic-only S1C39::M-HOLD-120 experiment.

Preparation, dehydration, storage, and prior melt-residence histories must be frozen and matched because E2 showed large realization-state variation and M-HOLD-120 does not itself control process state.
The repeat aggregation rule must be preregistered, including whether thresholds apply to every repeat, the repeat mean, or a confidence bound.
M-HOLD-120 supports phenomenological drift comparisons but cannot establish a molecular encounter-frequency mechanism or prove that the acrylic axis controls only viscosity level.
Any later use of M-ANCHOR or reconstructed 120-130 C response in resin-modified chemistry remains unsupported until a direct M-SWEEP verifies thermal-shape transferability.
robustness_adjudication.skeptic_objection_reasoning: The strongest objection is decisive for experiment ordering: the proposed 7.61% H-CORE comparator transfers E1's single measured drift coefficient from an NCO:OH 1.7 formulation to the unmeasured E2-derived NCO:OH 1.8 core. A direct hold on S1C41 would still provide a valid SI_15_60 observation, but departure from 7.61% could not be uniquely attributed to superlinear modifier suppression. The first experiment should therefore be the reactive-core-only E2 lattice card S1C09::M-HOLD-120, which directly establishes the undiluted comparator under the same hold protocol. This scientific prerequisite is not encoded in the VOI score and outweighs the deterministic ranking. Subsequent matched S1C39 and S1C41 holds would still be needed to distinguish acrylic-only suppression from tackifier-required H-DUAL behavior.
robustness_adjudication.weight_sensitivity_assessment: The tied top set was unchanged in all 25 tested scenarios: each individual weight was scaled from 0.5 to 1.5, no flipped scenarios occurred, and every recommendation_flip_boundary reports survival across the entire sweep. The base margin to the first strictly lower card is 0.004583. Thus no tested perturbation causes S1C41::M-HOLD-120 to cease being top ranked. Weightings outside the tested range were not evaluated. The preferred departure below is not supported by reweighting; it is supported by the unencoded scientific prerequisite identified by the Skeptic.

skeptic.chemistry_domain_support_assessment: The primary SI_15_60 observable stays within the support of the actual measurement because it is directly measured on S1C41 and does not depend on the shared thermal-response shape. S1C41 is nevertheless outside the chemistry support for M-ANCHOR or any reconstructed 120-130 C response. A direct M-SWEEP would be required before transferring that shape to the resin-modified family, but it is not a prerequisite for the proposed direct hold measurement.
skeptic.falsification_criterion_assessment: The instrument protocol can directly produce SI_15_60 values below 3.80% or at/above 7.61%, so the stated numerical criterion is operationally reachable. The repeat aggregation rule should be frozen in advance. Scientific falsification of H-CORE is still conditional on validating the E1-derived baseline for the E2 core; H-RESIN versus H-DUAL cannot be falsified comparatively by this single dual-axis card.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Drift below 3.80% could not cleanly falsify a reactive-core-only rule for the E2 core, because the undiluted E2 drift coefficient is unknown and may differ from E1 because of stoichiometry or core composition.
objections.objection: The claimed H-CORE prediction of 7.61% is calculated as E1_drift (9.51%) times the S1C41 reactive mass fraction (0.8000), but E1 has NCO:OH = 1.7 while S1C41 retains the E2 core with NCO:OH = 1.8. The payload explicitly states that no E2 thermal-hold trajectory has been measured. Thus the experiment tests an E1-to-E2-core transfer assumption in addition to linear dilution. The numerical H-CORE versus suppression separation is 7.608% minus 3.804% = 3.804 percentage points, which does exceed the declared 2.00-point resolution, but that resolution does not cure the unverified reference transfer.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A low S1C41 result could support generic resin suppression but could not establish that TK100 is specifically required or that AC1920 principally controls only viscosity level.
objections.objection: A single dual-axis S1C41 hold cannot establish H-DUAL's registered support condition that low drift occurs only when the minor-tackifier axis is nonzero. The proposer correctly lists H-RESIN versus H-DUAL as unseparated and calls for an acrylic-only hold. The claimed H-CORE versus H-DUAL separation is only a pointwise prediction contrast at the dual-axis composition, not a complete adjudication of the tackifier-required hypothesis.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Any observed suppression could be incorrectly assigned to TK100 specialization, AC1920, total nonreactive fraction, or an AC1920-TK100 interaction.
objections.objection: S1C41 simultaneously introduces 15.0 wt% AC1920, 5.0 wt% TK100, and reduces the reactive-core fraction to 0.8000. Therefore the measured SI_15_60 cannot attribute suppression separately to acrylic-like modification, minor-tackifier-like modification, their interaction, or simple dilution. In particular, the proposed experiment cannot distinguish H-RESIN's general resin effect from H-DUAL's tackifier-specific effect.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Repeat differences or apparent departures from the 3.80% and 7.61% thresholds could be caused by preparation state rather than formulation-level drift behavior.
objections.objection: The selected M-HOLD-120 card has process_state_risk_detail.score = 0.75, controls_process_state = false, and six missing process fields. The catalog protocol specifies two independent repeats but does not itself prescribe matched dehydration, storage, preparation, and prior melt-residence histories. This is important because E2 nominal preparations showed 46-58% viscosity-level CV and a 3.57-fold max/min ratio at 120 C.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: No primary claim is weakened on this ground, provided all threshold decisions use the directly measured repeat-level SI_15_60 values rather than a fitted time trajectory.
objections.objection: The primary observable survives this attack surface: SI_15_60 is calculated directly from measured eta_15 and eta_60 values during the same 120 C hold. It requires no regression, extrapolation, shared-shape reconstruction, or imputation.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: There is no chemistry-domain invalidation of the direct drift observable; the problem would arise only if viscosity level or 120-130 C response were reconstructed from the unmodified-family shape.
objections.objection: S1C41 is resin-modified and therefore outside the unmodified PPG2000/PDP70/MDI family supporting the shared thermal-response shape, but the selected M-HOLD-120 protocol does not reuse that shape. The proposer explicitly disallows M-ANCHOR-based inference before direct verification, consistent with the advisory audit.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: Discordant repeats could be adjudicated after seeing results, and a nominal H-CORE falsification could instead reflect an incorrect E1-to-E2 baseline.
objections.objection: The numerical criteria are attainable because M-HOLD-120 can directly return drift below 3.80% or at/above 7.61%. However, the phrase 'across at least two repeats' does not specify whether every repeat, the repeat mean, or a confidence bound must cross the threshold. More importantly, falsification of H-CORE remains conditional on the unsupported use of E1's 9.51% coefficient for the E2-derived core.

objections.consequence_if_ignored: A rheological drift result could be overstated as proof of a molecular encounter-frequency mechanism or axis specialization that was not measured.
objections.objection: No target hold result or hidden validation outcome is visibly used. However, M-HOLD-120 can establish only phenomenological suppression relative to a comparator; it cannot establish H-RESIN's stated molecular explanation that modifiers lower effective concentration and encounter frequency of reaction-capable species, nor H-DUAL's assertion that the acrylic axis principally relocates viscosity level.

skeptic.recommended_change: Run a matched M-HOLD-120 set rather than S1C41 alone: include an E2 reactive-core-only card to measure the undiluted drift coefficient under the same preparation history, retain S1C41::M-HOLD-120, and add the payload acrylic-only S1C39::M-HOLD-120 at 15% AC1920 to test whether low drift occurs without TK100. Freeze process-history controls and specify whether thresholds apply to every repeat, the repeat mean, or a confidence bound.
skeptic.strongest_objection: The 7.61% H-CORE comparator transfers the single E1 hold coefficient from an NCO:OH = 1.7 core to an unmeasured E2-derived NCO:OH = 1.8 core. Without a matched E2-core hold, departure from 7.61% cannot be uniquely assigned to superlinear modifier suppression.

tool_trace.name: get_chemistry_audited_rheology_summary
tool_trace.reason: Mandatory first action: candidate or experiment ranking is not admissible until the chemistry-provenance-audited upstream rheology, shared-shape support, state-shift evidence, hold contrast, and E1 +P perturbation check are loaded.

claim_boundaries: The shared-shape/state-shift structure is established only within the measured local chemistry family.
The apparent E_eta descriptor is rheological, not a chemical reaction activation energy.
The E1/E5 hold contrast does not identify a unique molecular mechanism.
The verified E1 +P phosphoric-acid perturbation is excluded from the primary same-composition fit and is interpreted separately as a chemical-perturbation check.
No validation-formulation identity or outcome is used by this tool.
design_rules: Represent a candidate as formulation plus process/realization state, not composition alone.

Use one state-specific anchor measurement to locate a new realization or nearby local formulation on the transferable thermal-response shape when it remains inside the supported local chemistry family.
Treat static viscosity, temperature response and thermal-hold stability as separate decision variables.
When the failure mode is hot-hold drift, choose an experiment and measurement window that directly test drift rather than only matching one nominal viscosity value.
Use external resin/tackifier evidence to define chemically plausible directions, but do not convert analogue proximity into a predicted local outcome.
Keep deliberately chemistry-perturbed curves outside same-composition fitting, but use them to test whether an intervention shifts viscosity scale, thermal-response shape, or both.

chemical_perturbation_check.interpretation: The verified low-dose H3PO4 perturbation shifts the observed viscosity level while remaining closely compatible with the local shared thermal-response geometry. It is a separate chemical-perturbation check and is not pooled into the primary same-composition state model.

observational_E1_R01_day1_comparator.interpretation_boundary: Observational reference only; the compact record does not establish a paired parent-batch relationship between E1 +P and E1 R01 day-1.

one_point_state_calibration.interpretation: Within the tested local chemistry family, one state-specific viscosity anchor can locate a previously held-out nominal formulation on the shared thermal-response shape to roughly 6-10% pooled multiplicative error.
one_point_state_calibration.validation_scheme: leave one nominal formulation out; fit shared shape on the remaining formulations; use one anchor from the held formulation

state_shift_master_curve.interpretation: Within the chemistry-audited local family, a realization-specific viscosity-scale intercept plus a shared quadratic inverse-temperature response closes the data far better than a formulation-level intercept using the same thermal basis.

temporal_stability_coordinate.interpretation: Original E1 and E5 hold trajectories show that thermal-hold viscosity drift is strongly formulation dependent and should be treated separately from static viscosity.

thermal_coordinate.interpretation: The apparent temperature-sensitivity descriptor remains comparatively concentrated after chemistry auditing; it is a rheological descriptor, not a molecular reaction activation energy.

experiment_design_implications.hold_window: For the current local study, 120 C and the common 15-60 min window directly interrogate the observed instability while matching the available validation window.
experiment_design_implications.selection_target: Select a formulation-process point that is informative about the observed instability and state uncertainty, not merely the closest static-viscosity value.
experiment_design_implications.state_anchor: A single in-range anchor can be used for efficient local curve calibration; 120 C is operationally attractive because it is also the hold-stability test temperature.
experiment_design_implications.verified_acid_perturbation: E1 +P received 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution during dehydration. Its close agreement with the primary shared thermal shape makes it useful as a defined scale-versus-shape perturbation check, not as another nominal E1 realization.

provenance_audit.reason: E1 +P is a verified chemical perturbation: 0.025 mmol H3PO4 from a 0.1 mol/L standard solution was added during dehydration. It is excluded from the same-composition primary state model and exposed separately as a perturbation check.

result.claim_boundary: External examples are analogues. They support candidate-family and coarse-region hypotheses, not an exact optimum for AC1920/TK100 and not a proven local molecular mechanism. The current reconstruction uses only pre-result evidence at runtime; the exact validation coordinates and outcome are excluded from candidate construction, ranking and tie-breaking.

decision_policy.claim_boundary: This policy can recover an evidence-supported formulation neighborhood, but it is not a predictor of the exact wet-lab optimum.

acrylic_like.basis: 15% directional lower-region evidence plus directly commensurate ~19-20% examples; 25% remains directly supported but is a larger perturbation.

minor_tackifier_like.basis: Curated PUR examples repeatedly place tackifying/hydrocarbon resin near 5%, with broader guidance below about 10%.

experiment_intents.causal_isolation: Use when the primary objective is attribution of one formulation axis. Prefer a single active modifier axis only in this mode.
experiment_intents.performance_mitigation: Use when a measured failure mode is already established and the next experiment is intended to reduce that failure. Independently supported multi-modifier interventions are admissible.
experiment_intents.uncertainty_resolution: Use when missing process, stoichiometric or evidence information prevents an interpretable performance test.

decision_policy.purpose: Select an experimentally informative intervention from pre-result evidence without treating a literature composition as the hidden optimum.
ranking_rules: Exact distance to an external analogue anchor is audit metadata, not a primary optimization objective.
Candidates in the same evidence-support class are not rewarded merely for being numerically closer to a literature percentage.
For performance mitigation, two modifier axes may be combined when each is independently supported and the combination stays inside bounded evidence regions.

Among candidates with comparable evidence coverage and interpretability, prefer the smallest sufficient total modifier burden and the smallest justified departure from the characterized local chemistry.
A single-variable design is preferred only when causal attribution is the stated experiment intent; it is not a universal default.
Held-out validation coordinates and outcomes must never enter candidate construction, ranking or tie-breaking.

historical_status.interpretation: The prospective historical claim attaches to the Agent recommendation itself. The current coarse grid and fine-refinement software are later reproducible operationalizations of the evidence-constrained region and are not represented as the original contemporaneous freeze algorithm unless older provenance is recovered.

chemistry_applicability_audit.enforcement_note: In this condition the chemistry applicability audit is ADVISORY. Every experiment card above remains selectable, including the cards the audit marks inadmissible. Use the audit as scientific evidence and justify whatever you select.
rule_text: Scope: measurement admissibility, not formulation admissibility.
M-HOLD-120, M-REPEAT and M-SWEEP observe their quantity directly and remain admissible.

M-ANCHOR is admissible only when assess_shared_shape_applicability returns shared_shape_use == 'allowed_with_state_anchor', or when a versioned prior direct sweep has verified transferability for the same chemistry family.
Otherwise M-ANCHOR is inadmissible_before_shape_verification: the one-point anchor would reconstruct 120-130 C viscosity through a shape that has never been measured for that chemistry.
This audit is a deterministic scientific rule, not a VOI penalty and not a model opinion. Whether it is binding in this run is stated by the enforcement field.

voi.formula: VOI = w_hyp * hypothesis_discrimination + w_unc * uncertainty_reduction + w_dec * decision_relevance + w_int * measurement_interpretability - w_ext * extrapolation_risk - w_proc * process_state_risk. Every component is normalized to [0, 1] by construction. This is a transparent normalized score with reported weight sensitivity, not a Bayesian posterior.
voi.tie_note: These experiments share an identical component vector. The deterministic tool is indifferent among them. Any choice within this set must be justified scientifically.

top_cards.acceptance_criterion: Matched 15-60 min drift at 120 C stays below 3.80% across at least two repeats, i.e. below half the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61% implied by a reactive mass fraction of 0.8000. This accepts H-RESIN over H-CORE.
top_cards.admissibility_reason: The matched-window 120 C hold observes thermal-hold drift directly and does not reuse the shared thermal-response shape, so it stays admissible outside the validated chemistry family.
top_cards.falsification_criterion: H-RESIN is falsified if matched 15-60 min drift is at or above the linear-dilution prediction of 7.61%. H-CORE is falsified if drift falls below 3.80%, a separation larger than the 2.00% resolution threshold. This composition carries both axes, so it cannot separate H-RESIN from H-DUAL; an acrylic-only hold is the follow-up required for that.
